claims.statement: Split-reservation logic in allocation rule v18 is the root cause of order holdups: 100% of 186 held orders are in the EXC-0921 scope (v18 split-reserved orders routed to east node); no held orders exist outside this scope
claims.corroboration: Exception audit confirms perfect correlation: EXC-0921 scope = all held orders. Rule v18 is the only production change since last week. Timing aligns (v18 live 22:00, issues reported 06:00+). Limitation: cannot yet distinguish v18-logic defect from carrier-side rejection of valid split reservations or inventory-count drift on east node.
claims.limitation: Awaiting carrier ops confirmation and inventory count inspection to rule out carrier-side or inventory causes

claims.statement: Customer impact: 186 orders with delayed delivery, generating ongoing support escalations; exact SLA/revenue impact requires quantification
claims.corroboration: Monitor shows 9% of overnight allocations held for >90min on east node. Support reports continuous arrivals. EXC-0921 audit confirms scope and ownership.
claims.limitation: Total revenue/SLA impact not yet quantified; cannot estimate escalation cascade without impact_estimate artifact

next_action.rationale: Discriminating evidence: are east-node carriers rejecting or not receiving the split-reserved orders? This distinguishes between allocation-defect (bad reservations), carrier-lag (rejecting valid ones), and inventory-drift (unable to fulfill).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Carrier-side confirmation will rule out or confirm carrier_feed_lag mechanism and establish whether the issue is inbound (reservation logic) or outbound (carrier acceptance)
